"""
Task 012 — Parse a date string

Interprets the spec as: support common date formats that users might type,
including ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD), long month name formats, short month name
formats, and other common separators (/, .). Raises ValueError for unparseable input.
"""

from datetime import datetime


def parse_date(s: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """Parse a date string and return (year, month, day)."""
    if not s or not s.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"Cannot parse empty date string: {repr(s)}")

    s = s.strip()

    # List of formats to try, in order of likelihood
    formats = [
        "%Y-%m-%d",       # 2024-03-15
        "%Y/%m/%d",       # 2024/03/15
        "%Y.%m.%d",       # 2024.03.15
        "%B %d, %Y",      # March 15, 2024
        "%B %d %Y",       # March 15 2024
        "%b %d, %Y",      # Mar 15, 2024
        "%b %d %Y",       # Mar 15 2024
        "%d %B %Y",       # 15 March 2024
        "%d %b %Y",       # 15 Mar 2024
        "%d-%B-%Y",       # 15-March-2024
        "%d-%b-%Y",       # 15-Mar-2024
        "%m/%d/%Y",       # 03/15/2024
        "%d/%m/%Y",       # 15/03/2024
        "%m-%d-%Y",       # 03-15-2024
        "%d.%m.%Y",       # 15.03.2024
        "%m.%d.%Y",       # 03.15.2024
        "%B %Y",          # March 2024 (day=1)
        "%b %Y",          # Mar 2024 (day=1)
        "%Y %B %d",       # 2024 March 15
        "%Y %b %d",       # 2024 Mar 15
        "%d %B, %Y",      # 15 March, 2024
        "%d %b, %Y",      # 15 Mar, 2024
    ]

    for fmt in formats:
        try:
            dt = datetime.strptime(s, fmt)
            return (dt.year, dt.month, dt.day)
        except ValueError:
            continue

    raise ValueError(f"Cannot parse date string: {repr(s)}")
